newsitem.title: USA: Judge refuses McDougal's request to stay free.
newsitem.headline: Judge refuses McDougal's request to stay free.

text.p: A federal judge on Monday denied a request by James McDougal, the former Whitewater partner of President Bill Clinton, to remain free while he appeals a conviction on fraud and conspiracy charges.
McDougal, 56, had won prosecutors' support for his petition but U.S. District Judge George Howard turned it down and he must now report to prison to begin serving his three-year sentence on June 16.
"The motion for bond pending appeal has been denied," Howard said in his ruling, adding that he did not think the appeal would result in a reversal of McDougal's conviction or a new trial.
McDougal was last year convicted on 18 counts of fraud and conspiracy but escaped a heavier sentence because he then began cooperating with Whitewater independent prosecutor Kenneth Starr.

He has reportedly corroborated allegations that Clinton pressured an Arkansas banker to extend an illegal $300,000 loan to James McDougal's former wife Susan McDougal in 1986, when Clinton was governor of Arkansas.
Prosecutors allege that about $50,000 of the proceeds of that loan were funneled into the failing Whitewater real estate venture in which the McDougals were partners of Bill and Hillary Clinton.
